thread.title: Stocks Down; Apple Heads For 7th Weekly Loss In A Row

author: EdJenner
title: Stocks Down; Apple Heads For 7th Weekly Loss In A Row
text:
Small caps kept their losses small but the major indexes reversed to sizable losses in late morning trade Wednesday. Meanwhile, Apple ( AAPL ), which has become a market proxy for many investors, slid 2%.
X
Apple is on track for its seventh weekly loss in a row, something the stock hasn’t done since six years ago.
On Wednesday, the small cap Russell 2000 fell 0.2%%, after being up 1% early. The Nasdaq, S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average each lost 0.6%.
Volume fell on the NYSE but grew on the Nasdaq vs. the same time Tuesday. Apple As Market Proxy
Apple’s status as a stock market proxy is based on its size, its long-term performance, its weighting in the averages and its attractiveness to both growth and value oriented fund managers.
Apple’s current decline might spark hopes of a rebound, but investors need to be careful. From late September 2012 to mid-November 2012, Apple dropped eight weeks in a row. A 17% rebound off the low followed in the next two weeks, but then Apple resumed its decline. The stock eventually dropped 45% off its high.
Apple is 19% off its high now.
Among IBD’s 197 industry groups, oil stocks and apparel did well as the stock market approached its midsession mark.
Oil stock prices have dropped as the price of crude oil slides. Light sweet crude hit a closing high Oct. 3. Since then, the price of a barrel of oil fell about 27%. Different Stories In Oil Patch
However, IBD’s 10 industry groups in the oil patch tell different stories. The pipeline stocks, which are less sensitive to oil and natural gas prices, have corrected only about 10%. The integrated stocks, which are somewhat diversified within the oil space, are down only 13%.
Chevron ( CVX ), an integrated oil stock, eased 0.1% late Wednesday morning. The stock is only 14% off its high. Compare that to explorer Cimarex Energy ( XEC ), which is 33% off its high. Cimarex added 2% Wednesday morning. Marijuana Stocks Off
On the downside, specialty consumer stocks, which includes marijuana stocks , were hammered.
Marijuana losers for the day included Canopy Growth ( CGC ), off about 11%; Tilray ( TLRY ), 9%; Cronos Group ( CRON ), 5%; and Aphria ( APHA ), 8%. Aphria is a Nov. 2 initial public offering.
None of the marijuana stocks are near a buy point. Cronos has the best Composite Rating, 78. The Composite Rating combines all five IBD ratings into a single number. A rating of 78 means 22% of all the stocks in IBD’s database rate higher.
